description:
Works related to existing driveway area “car port”
After advice given on site meeting with council of Hillingdon planning enforcement officer I would like to submit application for the driveway roof in order to park the car or van securely.
decision_conditions: The proposed car port, by reason of its design, scale, depth and overall bulk, would result in an incongruous and visually intrusive form of development that would fail to harmonise with the architectural composition, proportions and character of the host dwelling. Furthermore, its prominent siting and material pallet would appear out of character with the established pattern of development and prevailing built form within the street scene, to the detriment of the visual amenities of the area, contrary to Policy BE1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part One - Strategic Policies (2021), Policies DMHB 11, DMHB 12 and DMHD 1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management (2020), Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021) and Chapter 12 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The development fails to demonstrate that sufficient, policy-compliant off-street parking provision can be provided and retained within the site. The as-built car port does not reflect the approved dimensions, the existing garage is no longer practically accessible for parking, and the site's PTAL rating of 1b indicates a high reliance on private vehicles. The proposal would therefore be likely to result in increased on-street parking, congestion and harm to pedestrian safety. Furthermore, the proposal includes doors shown to open outward over the public footway, which is unlawful under the Highways Act 1980 and would be detrimental to highway and pedestrian safety. The proposed development is therefore considered to be contrary to Policy DMT 2 of Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2, Development Management Policies (2020) and London Plan (2021) Policy T4 and the Council's 2022 Domestic Vehicle Footway Crossover Policy, as well as the NPPF, in particular Paragraph 116.

In dealing with the application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive way. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies from the  Local Plan Part 1, Local Plan Part 2, Supplementary Planning Documents, Planning Briefs and other informal written guidance, as well as offering a full pre-application advice service.

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan - The Spatial Development Strategy for London consolidated with alterations since 2011 (2016) and national guidance.
